- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending flat or slightly down, model overestimates upward momentum; reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10+ consecutive days show price > 1.5σ above mean, model tends to overpredict continuation; apply downward bias of 2–5% per 3-day window.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% upward adjustment in final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.23, -0.11, +0.23), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment sign shift lagged by 2–3 days.
